briefs.headline: Liverpool beat 10-man Manchester United 4-0 in Pochettino's first match in charge
briefs.summary: Liverpool defeated Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday in Mauricio Pochettino's first match as United's coach, per ESPN's match report and box score. Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for denying Alexander Isak an obvious goal-scoring opportunity just outside the box; Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free kick in the 10th, Florian Wirtz hooked in Rio Ngumoha's cross in the 13th, Ngumoha scored in the 66th from Bradley Barcola's pass on a break and substitute Victor Munoz added the fourth in the 82nd from a Wirtz through ball. Liverpool had 28 shots and 11 on target to United's 10 and three, with 63.8% of possession, and Senne Lammens made seven saves. Liverpool move to fourth on 21 points from 11 matches; United are 19th on 8 and have gone nine league matches without a win, per ESPN's report. Liverpool play at Everton on Sunday at 7 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Burrow carries no designation as the Bengals play at Washington tonight
briefs.summary: The Bengals play at Washington tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN seeking a sixth straight win. Joe Burrow, listed with an illness, was a full participant in all three practices last week and carries no game-status designation on the club's final injury report, per Bengals.com; right guard Dalton Risner (knees) is out and linebacker Oren Burks is on injured reserve, cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring) and receiver Andrei Iosivas (thumb) are doubtful, and safety Kyle Dugger, guards Dylan Fairchild and Brian Parker II, linebacker Swayze Bozeman and cornerback Dax Hill, who missed the week with an illness, are questionable. Washington lists center Lucas Patrick (concussion), cornerback Amik Robertson and running backs Rachaad White and Jacory Croskey-Merritt as questionable. ESPN's preview has Burrow completing 74.7% of his passes, second in the league with 2,795 yards and first with 27 touchdown passes, against a Washington defense that blitzes on 42.1% of opposing drop-backs, the league's third-highest rate. Cincinnati has seven wins and two losses and leads the AFC North; Washington has three wins, five losses and a tie after beating the Giants.

briefs.headline: Crew's Game 2 against Inter Miami is set for Friday at 8 p.m. ET in Columbus
briefs.summary: ESPN's MLS schedule, read this morning, lists Game 2 of the Columbus Crew's best-of-three first-round series against Inter Miami for Friday, Nov. 27, at 8 p.m. ET at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in Columbus on FS1 and Apple TV; the kickoff time was not listed when Sunday's paper went out. Columbus lead the series one game to none after Saturday's 3 to 0 win in Miami, in which Gonzalo Tapia scored twice and Miami played the second half a man down, and advance to the conference semifinals with a second win; a Miami win forces a deciding Game 3. In Sunday's other Game 1s, Charlotte won 2 to 1 at Chicago and Vancouver won 2 to 0 over Real Salt Lake.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati beat Nashville 1-0 on an own goal to open the first-round series
briefs.summary: FC Cincinnati defeated Nashville SC 1-0 at Geodis Park on Sunday in Game 1 of their best-of-three MLS Cup Playoffs first-round series, per ESPN's match report and box score, handing the Supporters' Shield winners their first home loss of a season in which they went 15-0-2 there. Nashville midfielder Patrick Yazbek, under pressure in the seventh minute, tried to play back to goalkeeper Brian Schwake, who was off his line, and curled the ball into his own net. Roman Celentano made six saves for his fourth clean sheet of the season as Nashville had 23 shots and 68.7% of possession to Cincinnati's five shots; Hany Mukhtar hit the crossbar in the 63rd and a Sam Surridge goal in the 75th was ruled out for offside. Nashville set league records this season with 77 points, 23 wins and three losses. Game 2 is Saturday at 6:30 p.m. ET at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Apple TV, and a Cincinnati win ends the series.

briefs.headline: Onosato sets an 80-win target for 2027 as the Hatsu basho sits 48 days out
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato told a press conference at his stable's Fukuoka lodgings on Monday, a day after winning the Kyushu basho (tournament) in a playoff for his second straight yusho (championship) and his seventh overall, that it was his first Kyushu title and "a very fresh feeling," the Mainichi Shimbun reported via Yahoo News Japan. He said the left shoulder he dislocated at last year's Kyushu basho, which cost him this year's spring and summer tournaments, had left him "close to rock bottom" and unable to see his own sumo, that he now thinks his sumo is complete, and that he is aiming for 80 wins in 2027 and the year's most-wins title. The Yokozuna Deliberation Council, the Japan Sumo Association's advisory body, met in Tokyo on Monday, and chairman Tadamori Oshima said members felt Onosato had fulfilled a yokozuna's responsibility and dignity and that they would rather commend yokozuna Hoshoryu for finishing nine wins and six losses after his early defeats, Nikkan Sports reported; he said the council wants both yokozuna contesting the title on the final day next year. The JSA's tournament schedule lists the Hatsu basho at the Kokugikan in Tokyo from Sunday, Jan. 10, through Jan. 24, 2027, 48 days from today, with the banzuke (rankings) released Dec. 21; the JSA's English champions interview page for Kyushu was still unposted at 5:52 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Eagles beat the Steelers 19-16 to end a seven-game skid and drop Pittsburgh to 6-4
briefs.summary: Philadelphia defeated Pittsburgh 19-16 at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday before 69,879, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, ending the Eagles' seven-game losing streak, their longest in 14 years, and keeping the Steelers winless in Philadelphia since 1965; Jake Elliott kicked 53- and 55-yard field goals in the second half, and Aaron Rodgers went 30 of 44 for 227 yards with a 20-yard touchdown pass to Max Hurleman with 1:21 left. Pittsburgh is 6-4 and third in the AFC North behind Cincinnati and Cleveland. Carolina won 35-33 over Baltimore on Ryan Fitzgerald's 37-yard field goal with 1:44 left, a sixth straight loss for the 4-7 Ravens; San Francisco won 35-10 over Minnesota in Mexico City before 85,612 as Brock Purdy threw three first-half touchdown passes, and Buffalo won 26-9 over Miami to reach 9-1. Denver won 38-24 over Las Vegas, the Raiders' third straight loss before they visit Cleveland on Sunday night; Chicago won 21-13 over New Orleans, the Bengals' visitors next Sunday; Detroit won 31-21 over Tampa Bay, Kansas City won 34-7 over Arizona, Dallas won 51-30 over Tennessee, the New York Giants won 23-18 over Jacksonville and the Jets won 27-24 at the Chargers.

briefs.headline: Jokic and Murray carry the Nuggets past the Bulls 151 to 145 in overtime
briefs.summary: Denver won 151 to 145 in overtime at Chicago on Sunday night before 19,360, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story, as Nikola Jokic had 37 points, 18 rebounds and 11 assists for the 202nd triple-double of his career, seven short of Russell Westbrook's record, and Jamal Murray scored a season-high 45, eight of them in overtime. Josh Giddey had 23 points, 14 rebounds and a career-high 22 assists for the Bulls, the first Chicago player past 20 assists in a game since 1985, and Buddy Hield scored 33. Golden State won 88 to 87 over Boston, a fourth straight loss for the Celtics despite Jayson Tatum's 27 points; Miami won 123 to 113 over Oklahoma City for a seventh straight win behind Bam Adebayo's 24 points, 15 rebounds and 12 assists, with both teams short-handed, per the AP. Atlanta won 107 to 97 over Detroit, New York won 113 to 106 over Indiana for a fifth straight win, Dallas won 116 to 114 at Utah and Washington won 116 to 96 over Orlando. San Antonio and the Lakers, level at 14 wins and three losses atop the West, were idle.

briefs.headline: Jacobsen's shot with 0.4 seconds left gives No. 24 Nebraska a 76-74 win over Butler
briefs.summary: Cale Jacobsen banked in a contested shot in the lane with 0.4 seconds left to give No. 24 Nebraska a 76-74 win over Butler in Chicago on Sunday in the Bad Boy Mowers Series, per ESPN's box score and the AP game story; Braden Frager and Damon Wilkinson scored 17 each for the Huskers, who are 6-0 and have won 30 straight non-conference games, and Asim Djulovic scored 28 for Butler, now 4-3. Among the other ranked teams playing Sunday, No. 6 Texas won 97-61 over Southern Indiana, No. 7 UCLA won 85-48 over Delaware and No. 18 USC won 82-56 over Louisiana. West Virginia, Marshall and Ohio were idle; Ohio opens the Jacksonville Classic against New Mexico State on Tuesday at 11 a.m. ET, Marshall hosts Prairie View A&M on Wednesday at 4 p.m. ET and West Virginia plays North Carolina in Charlotte on Friday at 7 p.m. ET.

waters.reading: 83.8 cfs, 1.54 feet at 5:15 a.m., falling on flow against 92.1 cfs and steady on stage against 1.59 feet in the fetcher's 24-hour comparison.
waters.working: The gauge at Dyer reads 83.8 cfs and 1.54 feet, the fetcher's 24-hour comparison 92.1 cfs and 1.59 feet, so the river is down another eight cfs on the day and under 85 for the first time in the run of readings this paper has carried; the stage trend reads steady. At 84 cfs and clear it is a long-leader, small-fly problem, the fish on the pocket-water lies and the tailouts rather than the seams, and in late-November water the midday hours fish best once the sun is on it. A size 18 to 20 midge or a small Blue-winged Olive nymph under a soft indicator on a 12-foot leader through the slower pockets and the tailouts is the pattern, a stonefly nymph as the point fly in the deeper plunge pools where the larger fish hold in cold water, and a sculpin pattern swung tight to the undercut banks in the first and last hour of light. Water this thin and this clear asks for a longer cast, a finer tippet and an approach from downstream.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 24.88 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 24.64 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 24.9 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool with ordinary bank access, up about a quarter-foot on the fetcher's 24-hour comparison after a week of falling and reading steady, so the upper gauge has stopped dropping. The wing dams and the riprap are still showing rock and the water is clear enough to fish structure rather than the slack behind it: shad are the forage, so a white or shad-pattern swimbait or a lipless crankbait worked down the face of the wing dams and along the riprap is the pattern, slowed down for water that has seen a run of cold nights, with a jig and crawfish trailer on the slack side of the lock wall for the fish holding off the current. With the pool flat rather than falling, the fish spread back along the length of each dam instead of bunching at the channel end, so the whole face is worth covering. The R.C. Byrd tailwater itself is not gauged; this is the pool side.
waters.source: USGS 03201500 (Ohio River at Point Pleasant); config.SPORTSMAN_WATERS

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.02 feet at 5 a.m., steady against 25.99 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.0 ft — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Normal pool, within a few hundredths of the fetcher's 24-hour comparison and reading steady, so both gauges that bracket the dam are flat this morning and the river is holding pool. Below the dam the pattern is the structure the dam makes: skipjack and shad stack in the current below the gates, and a spoon or a heavy jig worked in the churn, or a live skipjack drifted along the current seams off the lock wall, is the hybrid and catfish setup; the riprap along the Huntington bank fishes a crawfish-colour jig on the slack side where the bank current breaks. Huntington is the downstream bracket, 30-odd river miles below the dam, not the tailwater reading, which the Corps publish and this pipeline cannot fetch.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 12:26 AM at 0.0 ft, high 6:41 AM at 4.4 ft, low 1:27 PM at 0.2 ft, high 7:00 PM at 3.3 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 5:39 AM at 5.8 ft, low 12:05 PM at -0.1 ft, high 5:55 PM at 4.1 ft, low 11:47 PM at -0.4 ft. Water 62.4F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:30 a.m. Moon waxing gibbous, 98% illuminated, 13.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 6:41 AM and 7:00 PM in the sound.
waters.working: All four of the sound's events fall inside Monday for once: the 12:26 AM low at 0.0 feet, the 6:41 AM high at 4.4 feet, the highest of the fortnight, the 1:27 PM low at 0.2 and the 7:00 PM high at 3.3. The sound lags the surf by 62 minutes on the morning high, 82 on the midday low and 65 on the evening high, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills. The morning ebb drops 4.2 feet from 6:41 to 1:27 and the afternoon flood climbs 3.1 feet to 7:00, and at waxing gibbous, 98% and 13.5 days the moon is a day short of full, which the file's age puts on Tuesday, so these are the biggest swings and the hardest inlet current of the fortnight. The water at Beaufort read 62.4F at 5:30 a.m., up 0.3 from Sunday's reading. Beach conditions: the NWS active-alerts feed read at 5:50 a.m. carries nothing for Coastal Pender or Coastal New Hanover, and NWS Wilmington's forecast for the Topsail zone has Monday mostly cloudy with patchy morning fog, a slight chance of light rain, highs in the upper 60s and north wind around 5 mph, going north 10 to 15 after midnight; the same office issued a Gale Watch at 1:36 a.m. for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles, northeast winds 25 to 35 knots with gusts to 45 and seas 8 to 13 feet possible from Tuesday afternoon through Thursday morning, so the calm beach and pier window is today and Tuesday morning. The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry report, a monthly, is dated Nov. 1 and is 22 days old, so it is the month's pattern and not this morning's conditions: East Coast Sports reports the piers taking red drum over 32 inches on the north end of the island, smaller reds and the occasional trout in the sound and the focus shifting to almost exclusive trout action as the weather cools; Native Son has the 5-to-8-foot seams in the main creeks as the trout target and cut bait the best bet for the reds inside; Speckled Specialist reports live shrimp under a cork as the best approach and 3/16-ounce jig heads with a soft plastic for artificials, trout in 4 to 16 feet with 4 to 8 the most common, black drum to 18 inches over structure; Carolina Flats has topwater for locating trout early, deeper holes later in the day, and soft plastics for reds on the oyster and grass banks in what it calls a last blitz before inshore bait thins; Jolly Roger Pier reports scattered speckled trout, Virginia mullet and spot on the bottom at night and bluefish thick early; Surf City Pier has pompano, black drum and croaker on the bottom. Tied to today's table and a sound in the low 60s: the whole morning ebb is in daylight, so red drum's window, the last of the fall, runs roughly 11 a.m. to the 1:27 low on a bottom that will drain the creek mouths hard, cut menhaden or a finger mullet on a quarter-ounce head a couple of feet off the creek-channel edges where the draining grass dumps bait, or a soft plastic on the oyster and grass banks as the water leaves them. Trout want the first of the afternoon flood once the sun has been on the flats, roughly 2 to 5 p.m., in the 4-to-8-foot creek-channel seams and along the ICWW channel edge on a 3/16-ounce jig head and a small soft plastic worked slowly, or a live shrimp under a popping cork drifted over the oyster bars at the creek mouths; the flooded-grass window for a weedless gold spoon is the hour before the 7:00 PM high, which now falls after dark, and the dock lights on the flood after that are the night trout water. Spot and sea mullet on bloodworm or shrimp on a two-hook bottom rig in the ICWW channel on the last of the flood, 5 to 7 p.m.; with no surf advisory and a 5 mph wind this morning, bluefish on a metal jig from the beach or the piers in the first light, before Tuesday's blow. Flounder are release only.
